events.reason: Surveillance colonoscopy one year after resection

documents.title: Colonoscopy report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
COLONOSCOPY 02/17/2022
Indication: surveillance one year after low anterior resection for rectal adenocarcinoma.
Sedation: monitored anesthesia care, reduced dose given cirrhosis.
Findings: Prep good. Cecum reached, appendiceal orifice and ileocecal valve photographed. Colorectal anastomosis intact and widely patent, no nodularity or ulceration. Remainder of colon normal. No polyps.
Impression: healthy anastomosis, no evidence of recurrence.
Recommendation: repeat colonoscopy in 3 years unless symptoms.

orders.reason: progressive dyspnea and dry cough, basilar crackles

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Rescheduled from April.
S: The cough from the winter never left. Dry, worse with talking, no blood, no fever or sweats. Over the same months he is more winded: now stops halfway up his stairs, used to do them in one go. Albuterol helps a little. No chest pain, no orthopnea beyond his usual pillow. No leg swelling beyond baseline.
O: Vitals as charted. Fine end-inspiratory crackles at both bases, which I did not hear in March. No wheeze. Fingertips look clubbed - he says they've been like that a while. Heart RRR. Abd soft, mild flank dullness. Edema trace.
A: Five months of progressive dyspnea and dry cough with bibasilar crackles and clubbing in a former shipyard boiler worker. Asbestos-related lung disease is high on the list; COPD alone doesn't fit the crackles.
P: Pulmonology referral (they will do imaging and full PFTs; he cannot have iodinated contrast). Continue tiotropium/albuterol. Return precautions for fever, worsening breathlessness.

conditions.note: asbestos-related pneumoconiosis; bilateral lower-lobe fibrosis, calcified pleural plaques

reports.text: PA and lateral views. Bilateral lower-lobe reticular fibrotic opacities. Bilateral pleural thickening with calcified pleural plaques. No focal consolidation, no effusion, no pneumothorax. Heart size normal. Mediastinal contours normal.
reports.conclusion: Bilateral lower-lobe fibrosis with pleural thickening and calcified pleural plaques, consistent with asbestos-related disease.

reports.text: Full pulmonary function testing: spirometry, lung volumes by plethysmography and diffusing capacity. FEV1 within normal limits. FVC decreased. FEV1/FVC ratio normal. Total lung capacity decreased. DLCO decreased. No significant bronchodilator response.
reports.conclusion: Restrictive pattern with reduced diffusing capacity. No obstruction.

documents.title: Pulmonology Consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
PULMONARY MEDICINE CONSULTATION
Date of service: 08/25/2022
Re: Peter Kimball, 66
Referring: primary care

He describes about six months of breathlessness that has steadily worsened, along with a dry cough. Decades of work in a shipyard as a boiler technician; he recalls insulation dust everywhere in the early years. Retired 2017. Former smoker, 40 pack-years, quit 2017. Known COPD on tiotropium and as-needed albuterol.
Allergies: sulfonamides, iodinated contrast (anaphylaxis).

Exam: clubbing of the fingers. Crackles at the end of inspiration over both lung bases. No wheeze. No accessory muscle use at rest.

Chest radiograph today: fibrotic change in both lower lobes, pleural thickening and calcified pleural plaques.
PFTs today: decreased TLC, FVC and DLCO with a normal FEV1 and a normal FEV1/FVC ratio - restriction with impaired gas transfer.

Impression: asbestosis (asbestos-related pneumoconiosis) with pleural plaque disease, explaining the progressive dyspnea and cough.
Plan: continue current inhalers. Counseled on the diagnosis, the relationship to his occupational exposure and the slow natural history. Repeat PFTs in 6-12 months. Vaccinations up to date per patient. Return sooner for worsening.
Pulmonary Medicine

Screening: colon - surveillance colonoscopy Feb clean, repeat 2025. Prostate - urology, PSA 0.1. Lung - followed by pulmonology.
Vaccines: high-dose flu and bivalent COVID booster today.
Exam: Crackles at both bases. Clubbing. Heart RRR. Abd soft, flank dullness. L medial ankle ulcer ~1.5 cm, wound clinic following. Feet otherwise intact, monofilament normal, DP/PT diminished.
Labs: CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c, UACR.
Plan: f/u 2-3 months.

documents.title: Lab results

events.reason: Rectal bleeding and change in bowel habit

conditions.label: Radiation proctitis
conditions.note: chronic; rectal telangiectasias, treated with argon plasma coagulation

documents.title: Gastroenterology consultation and colonoscopy
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
GASTROENTEROLOGY, 12/12/2022
Reason for visit: rectal bleeding and changed bowel habits.

Mr. Kimball, 66, had long-course pelvic chemoradiation for stage IIIB rectal adenocarcinoma, finishing about two years ago, followed by low anterior resection; he also had prostate-bed radiation in 2017. For roughly six months he has passed blood per rectum and has had more urgency, with some episodes of fecal incontinence.
Allergies: sulfonamides, iodinated contrast.

Exam: well-appearing. Digital rectal exam: firm, non-tender rectum, no mass felt.
Labs today: Hgb 10.2, MCV 92, WBC 7.0, platelets 250.

Colonoscopy (same day): numerous telangiectatic vessels in the rectum, oozing on contact. Anastomosis intact. No mass, ulcer or other mucosal lesion to suggest recurrent cancer. Argon plasma coagulation applied to the telangiectasias in the rectum with good hemostasis.

Impression: chronic radiation proctitis with bleeding causing normocytic anemia; no recurrence.
Plan: APC can be repeated if bleeding recurs. CBC in 4-6 weeks with PCP. Avoid straining; continue lactulose titration.
Gastroenterology

documents.title: Dermatology consultation
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
DERMATOLOGY CONSULTATION, 06/07/2023
Referred by primary care for a left lower-leg ulcer.

History: diabetic with peripheral arterial and venous disease, recently seen by pulmonology and gastroenterology. The ulcer on his left lower leg has been open for more than two years in spite of grafting; over recent months it has grown and become more painful. He has had no fever or chills.
Allergies: sulfonamides, iodinated contrast.

Exam: on the left medial lower leg, a 3 cm ulcer whose edges are raised and everted; the base bleeds easily when touched. The surrounding skin is indurated, with several keratotic areas. No palpable inguinal or popliteal lymph nodes. Remainder of the skin and general exam unremarkable.

Data: A1c 7.8%, fasting glucose 172 mg/dL, CBC unremarkable (drawn this week). Ankle-brachial index 0.7 on the left.

Procedure: punch biopsy from the ulcer edge, after consent; hemostasis with pressure; dressing.

Impression: chronic ulcer with features worrying for malignant transformation (Marjolin ulcer); also arterial insufficiency on the left contributes to poor healing.
Plan: biopsy pending; will call patient and PCP.
Dermatology

conditions.label: Squamous cell carcinoma of skin of left lower limb, including hip
conditions.note: Marjolin's ulcer arising in chronic venous ulcer, left medial lower leg

reports.text: Specimen: skin, left medial lower leg, ulcer edge, punch biopsy. Invasive well-differentiated squamous cell carcinoma with keratin pearl formation, arising at the edge of a chronic ulcer with surrounding scar. Carcinoma extends to the deep and peripheral edges of this biopsy.
reports.conclusion: Invasive squamous cell carcinoma arising in a chronic ulcer (Marjolin ulcer).

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: For about two months, more and more tired - naps every afternoon. Belly feels tighter, pants don't close. Has lost weight in spite of the belly: down about 8 lb since September by our scale. Appetite poor. No fever, chills or night sweats. No confusion per him; 3 BMs/day. No black stools, rectal bleeding rare. Taking diuretics as prescribed.
O: Vitals as charted. Thin, temporal wasting. Sclerae icteric, more than his usual. Abdomen distended with shifting dullness, mildly firm in the RUQ, non-tender. No asterixis. Edema 1+.
A: Progressive fatigue, ascites and weight loss with deeper jaundice in Child-Pugh C cirrhosis. Concerned about further decompensation or a new liver lesion; last surveillance US (May) was clean.
P: CMP, CBC, INR today. Called hepatology - they moved his visit up to 12/1 with ultrasound and AFP the same day. No diuretic change until they see him. ED if confused, fever, abdominal pain or bleeding.

orders.reason: Child-Pugh C cirrhosis with suspected HCC

documents.title: Hepatology visit letter
documents.author: hepatology
documents.body:
HEPATOLOGY, 12/01/2023
Dear colleague,
Thank you for moving Mr. Kimball up. He returns, now 67, with three months of increasing fatigue, a swelling abdomen and a 10-lb weight loss; he denies fever, chills or sweats. Background: decompensated cirrhosis (HCV cured 2018, prior alcohol), radiation proctitis after rectal cancer treatment, and a squamous cell carcinoma of the leg excised this summer.

Exam: cachectic. Jaundice of skin and sclerae. Distended abdomen with a fluid wave. A firm, irregular mass is palpable in the right upper quadrant.

Labs: Hgb 11.2, platelets 85, INR 1.6, total bilirubin 3.2, albumin 2.9, AST 80, ALT 75, alkaline phosphatase 120, AFP 400 ng/mL (previously under 10).
Ultrasound today: 5 cm heterogeneous, nodular mass in the right lobe; no biliary obstruction; moderate ascites.

Impression: suspected hepatocellular carcinoma on a background of Child-Pugh C cirrhosis.
Plan:
1. Multiphase MRI with gadolinium (anaphylaxis was to iodinated contrast) to characterize the lesion.
2. Referral to the transplant center: a single lesion of this size would fall within transplant criteria, and his liver function argues for transplant over other treatment.
3. Diuretics unchanged; diagnostic paracentesis not needed today (no fever, no pain).
I will copy you on the MRI.
Hepatology

conditions.label: Liver cell carcinoma
conditions.note: 5.0 cm right lobe, LI-RADS 5, within Milan criteria; liver transplant candidate

reports.study: MRI abdomen with and without contrast
reports.text: Multiphase MRI of the liver with gadolinium-based extracellular contrast. Right hepatic lobe: 5.0 x 4.6 cm mass with arterial phase hyperenhancement, washout on portal venous and delayed phases and an enhancing capsule. No other focal lesion. No tumor in the portal or hepatic veins. Liver nodular and shrunken. Ascites. No enlarged lymph nodes. No osseous lesion in the field.
reports.conclusion: 5.0 cm right lobe observation, LI-RADS 5 (definite hepatocellular carcinoma). No vascular invasion. Cirrhosis with ascites.
